lead: D-Wave / QBTS - the quantum breakthrough everyone is chasing
smaller: Tesla / TSLA - the Musk backlash dip the crowd keeps buying
Gold / GLD - the fear trade that outran bitcoin
Robinhood / HOOD - the broker turning retail into event traders
why_lead: On 18 March QBTS closed at 10.80 USD, up 100.74% over five sessions and 78.81% over 20, the largest surge among the retail-favourite names in the closing data, and the crowd's own headlines (Stocktwits on retail bracing for an exponential rally, Yahoo Finance on quantum stocks having their breakout moment) show the attention side of the same move.

The narrative is a single simple story, a breakthrough claim, with a dated pending catalyst in the feed (Nvidia's first-ever Quantum Day, inside the GTC week the feed dates from 18 to 21 March), which made it more coherent on that day's evidence than the Tesla dip, whose dip-buying evidence was as strong but more political and less tied to a dated event.
why_smaller: Tesla's 36.37% 20-session drawdown has the most explicit dip-buying headlines in the feed, but it is a brand-and-politics story rather than a single dated catalyst, so it is the strongest alternative to the lead.
Gold is the non-equity trade the evidence supports: gold futures are up 3.11% over 20 sessions while bitcoin is down 1.93%, and the record-high headline set is retail-facing.

Robinhood's prediction-markets hub is a distinct non-AI narrative with a dated launch on 17 and 18 March and a clear regulatory break risk, which keeps it separate from the quantum and Tesla equity trades.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir (PLTR): a surge headline tied to a US$19 million buyback conflicts with that session's close (-3.96%), and the stock is down 32.68% over 20 sessions, so there is no single-session evidence for a lead.

Rocket Lab (RKLB): leveraged-ETF launches and meme-stock framing are real, but the space narrative overlaps the quantum trade and the stock is down 35.18% over 20 sessions with no evidence of a retail bid.
Nebius (NBIS): a 46.60% 20-session drawdown and 'next Nvidia' framing, but the attention evidence is thin.
Intel (INTC): up 31.04% over five sessions after the CEO appointment, but the headlines are about the turnaround rather than a crowd narrative; used only as a sector Breaking Convention item.
Nuclear (OKLO, SMR): Stocktwits reported retail sentiment pulling back on the surge, which is fading attention rather than a lead.
Bridger Aerospace: a 1000% jump in retail chatter, but the ticker is not in the closing data, so no price or horizon can be used.
Hims & Hers (HIMS): an FDA warning drove a 46.17% 20-session drop; the trade is regulatory rather than a retail momentum narrative, so it is used only in the health-care block.
Silver (SLV): squeeze speculation on Seeking Alpha is thin, and SLV is up only 3.14% over 20 sessions.
Large-cap AI names (NVDA, AAPL): attention is high, but the moves are index-driven rather than speculative, so they fail the price-and-attention test.
